# Measuring success in the AI era

Google's answer to the myth that old metrics no longer work in the AI era was to measure success through metrics that matter to the business. For AI features, Google points to the Generative AI performance report in Search Console (launched 3 June 2026 and rolled out to all sites worldwide by 31 August 2026), which lists impressions, pages, countries, devices (Search only) and dates, with no click or query metrics. Author's view: the report's country breakdown helps compare AI visibility across markets, and Search Console, not site: queries or Google Trends, is where to judge a migration or Discover demand. Day 3 added detail and debate. Search Console's regular Performance report still counts AI Overviews and AI Mode traffic under the Web search type, while the generative AI report counts AI-surface impressions only, by page, country and device, and Google expects it to get richer; Google said fan-out queries are not added to Search Console (not in Google's docs). Google's published position (August 2025) is that total organic clicks are relatively stable, and its guidance is to judge visits by conversions and value, not clicks alone. Community speakers argued from the practitioner side that rankings and clicks no longer equal business outcomes, that traffic after an AI recommendation may arrive direct or through paid search, and, in one case study, that a niche article converted 10 times better than a comprehensive one with far more impressions (single cases, no published data). A second recording of Day 1 added more voices. Gary Illyes said the generative AI reporting launched with the generative AI control, starting with impressions only, and may expand; in the Q&A a Google panelist expected more AI reporting to launch, without a timeline or a promise, and Google said AI reporting should not simply mirror classic results, because users get more information before they click, so Google first has to work out which data is useful and actionable. Community speakers said the industry turned everything into a metric because budgets are approved on numbers, that most AI-visibility tracking copies rank tracking with invented prompts, and that one misplaced figure in an LLM-assisted data pipeline compounds downstream; one agency replaced monthly reports that took a workday each and went unread with an automated pipeline (data in, script, AI summary, dashboard). On Day 2 migration speakers advised merging both sites' analytics, comparing daily Search Console data and crawls with the pre-migration baseline and giving moved content its own baseline, and an international speaker warned that features often launch in some languages or countries first, so cross-market comparisons should not assume a feature is live everywhere. Author's view: after a migration, report indexing and traffic recovery separately, since they move on very different timescales.

## What to do

- Track AI-feature visibility in the Generative AI performance report, knowing it has no click or query data, and report success in business metrics.
- Compare the report's country breakdown with native-language spot checks of AI answers in each market.
- After a migration, judge success by the new domain's indexing and traffic in Search Console, not by site: queries on the old domain.
- Judge Discover visibility from the Discover performance report; Google Trends does not show Discover demand.
- Measure visits that follow AI answers in your own analytics, and report organic, direct and branded paid traffic, conversions and revenue side by side.
- When comparing markets, check that the search feature you compare is live in each language and country.

- **[Stage]** A community speaker ran a controlled test with a brand that had seen organic clicks drop: for a set period the only activity was work to raise the brand's AI visibility, with no external campaigns and no budget changes.
  <br><sub>`D3-C519` · Day 3, Lightning session L: Understanding SERPs and your users (speaker not identified)</sub>

- **[Stage]** A community speaker reported that a higher rate of recommendation in AI answers brought one brand a really significant uplift in inquiries during a controlled test, without giving a figure.
  <br><sub>`D3-C520` · Day 3, Lightning session L: Understanding SERPs and your users (speaker not identified)</sub>

- **[Stage]** A community speaker said the brand in the controlled test had a record month, the kind of real business value that business owners care about more than a dip in traffic.
  <br><sub>`D3-C521` · Day 3, Lightning session L: Understanding SERPs and your users (speaker not identified)</sub>

- **[Stage]** During a community speaker's controlled test, the brand's paid search click-through rate rose by 36% while the only activity was work to raise its AI visibility.
  <br><sub>`D3-C522` · Day 3, Lightning session L: Understanding SERPs and your users (speaker not identified)</sub>

- **[Stage]** In a community speaker's controlled test the brand's AI visibility was tracked across the main AI engines and was described as really strong early in the experiment (whether as a starting level or a gain was not said).
  <br><sub>`D3-C523` · Day 3, Lightning session L: Understanding SERPs and your users (speaker not identified)</sub>

- **[Stage]** In the same controlled test the brand's top-of-page share in paid search dropped, so a slight dip in paid click-through rate would have been expected rather than the 36% rise, a community speaker said.
  <br><sub>`D3-C524` · Day 3, Lightning session L: Understanding SERPs and your users (speaker not identified)</sub>

- **[Stage]** A community speaker advised SEOs to work with paid search teams to understand changes such as a rise in paid click-through rate and what impact SEO work may have had, since those teams may not credit SEO for it.
  <br><sub>`D3-C525` · Day 3, Lightning session L: Understanding SERPs and your users (speaker not identified)</sub>

- **[Stage]** A community speaker said the customer journey that starts in AI services still exists and only the direct attribution is missing, so SEOs should look at wider metrics they have not tracked before.
  <br><sub>`D3-C529` · Day 3, Lightning session L: Understanding SERPs and your users (speaker not identified)</sub>

- **[Stage]** A community speaker's simplified journey: an AI recommendation makes a visit more likely; the person may check the brand on social media or see it while scrolling, search the brand name, and later click it in a generic search because they know it.
  <br><sub>`D3-C530` · Day 3, Lightning session L: Understanding SERPs and your users (speaker not identified)</sub>

- **[Stage]** When a brand bids on its own name, people who search the brand after an AI recommendation may arrive through paid search rather than organic, so organic reporting loses that visit, a community speaker noted.
  <br><sub>`D3-C531` · Day 3, Lightning session L: Understanding SERPs and your users (speaker not identified)</sub>

- **[Stage]** Clicks are down for a lot of businesses but rarely tell the whole story, a community speaker summarised, advising SEOs to ask the paid search team for Google Ads click-through rate reports.
  <br><sub>`D3-C532` · Day 3, Lightning session L: Understanding SERPs and your users (speaker not identified)</sub>

- **[Stage]** A community speaker advised SEOs to report conversion rates and traffic by channel, not only organic clicks.
  <br><sub>`D3-C533` · Day 3, Lightning session L: Understanding SERPs and your users (speaker not identified) · consistent with Google docs · [AI features and your website](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features), [Top ways to ensure your content performs well in Google's AI experiences on Search](https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2025/05/succeeding-in-ai-search)</sub>

- **[Stage]** For the brand in a community speaker's controlled test, organic sessions in GA4 roughly halved while direct sessions stayed fairly stable (an uncertain reading; a change of about 2% was mentioned, direction unclear in the recording).
  <br><sub>`D3-C537` · Day 3, Lightning session L: Understanding SERPs and your users (speaker not identified)</sub>

- **[Stage]** A community speaker advised comparing the relative performance of channels and choosing new metrics to report, rather than judging SEO on organic sessions alone.
  <br><sub>`D3-C538` · Day 3, Lightning session L: Understanding SERPs and your users (speaker not identified)</sub>

- **[Stage]** A fully controlled test of AI visibility was possible for one brand only because it ran no other marketing activity, and is not viable for most brands, a community speaker said.
  <br><sub>`D3-C539` · Day 3, Lightning session L: Understanding SERPs and your users (speaker not identified)</sub>

- **[Stage]** A community speaker recommended picking areas of a business where testing is possible and measuring how AI visibility affects conversion rates and revenue there.
  <br><sub>`D3-C540` · Day 3, Lightning session L: Understanding SERPs and your users (speaker not identified)</sub>

## What Google's documentation says

- **[Docs]** Google's guide for generative AI features recommends the Generative AI performance report in Search Console for measuring how content performs in generative AI features on Google Search and Discover.
  <br><sub>`D1-C062` · Google Search Central · annotates Day 1, How Search works and where's AI? · is the documentation · [Optimizing your website for generative AI features on Google Search](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/ai-optimization-guide) · Extended by [D3-C535](../../40-sessions/day3/D3-S13-lightning-session-l-understanding-serps-and-your-users.md) · Used by `DEV-MON-07`, the glossary term *Generative AI performance report*</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's launch post for the Generative AI performance reports in Search Console (3 June 2026; rolled out to all sites worldwide by 31 August 2026) lists impressions, pages, countries, devices (Search only) and dates, and no click or query metrics.
  <br><sub>`D1-C124` · Search Central blog (3 June 2026) · annotates Day 1, How Search works and where's AI? · is the documentation · [Introducing Search Generative AI performance reports in Search Console](https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2026/06/gen-ai-performance-reports) · Repeated by [D1-C196](../../40-sessions/day1/D1-S02-what-s-new-in-the-world-of-search.md) · Extended by [D2-C607](../../40-sessions/day2/D2-S15-focusing-on-internationalisation-and-localisation.md) · Extended by [D3-C063](../../40-sessions/day3/D3-S03-making-sense-of-users-queries.md) · Repeated by [D3-C437](../../40-sessions/day3/D3-S12-inside-search-console-what-s-new-how-to-use-it.md) · Repeated by [D3-C439](../../40-sessions/day3/D3-S12-inside-search-console-what-s-new-how-to-use-it.md) · Extended by [D3-C495](../../40-sessions/day3/D3-S13-lightning-session-l-understanding-serps-and-your-users.md) · Extended by [D3-C542](../../40-sessions/day3/D3-S13-lightning-session-l-understanding-serps-and-your-users.md) · Used by `DEV-MON-07`, the glossary term *Generative AI performance report*</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's Search Console help says AI Mode groups the user's question into subtopics and searches for each one simultaneously, and that a follow-up question in AI Mode is essentially a new query.
  <br><sub>`D3-C093` · Google Search Console Help · annotates Day 3, Making sense of users' queries · is the documentation · [What are impressions, position, and clicks?](https://support.google.com/webmasters/answer/7042828?hl=en)</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's core updates page recommends waiting at least a full week after a core update has finished rolling out before analysing Search Console data, then comparing that week with a week before the update started.
  <br><sub>`D3-C272` · Google Search Central · annotates Day 3, What are quality updates · is the documentation · [Google Search's core updates and your website](https://developers.google.com/search/updates/core-updates)</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's launch post for Search Console's branded queries filter (20 November 2025) says the branded versus non-branded split is made by an internal AI-assisted system, not by a regular expression, and that some queries may occasionally be misidentified.
  <br><sub>`D3-C473` · Search Central blog (20 November 2025, updated 11 March 2026) · annotates Day 3, Lightning session L: Understanding SERPs and your users · is the documentation · [Introducing the branded queries filter in Search Console](https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2025/11/search-console-branded-filter) · Extends [D3-C417](../../40-sessions/day3/D3-S12-inside-search-console-what-s-new-how-to-use-it.md) · Used by the glossary term *Branded queries filter*</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's blog post on Search Console data limits says anonymized queries are always left out of the report tables but counted in chart totals unless you filter by query, and are left out whenever a filter is applied, so filtered rows do not add up to the chart totals.
  <br><sub>`D3-C481` · Search Central blog (19 October 2022) · annotates Day 3, Lightning session L: Understanding SERPs and your users · is the documentation · [A deep dive into Search Console performance data filtering and limits](https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2022/10/performance-data-deep-dive) · Used by `DEV-MON-08`</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's AI features guide says traffic from sites appearing in AI features such as AI Overviews and AI Mode is included in the overall search traffic in Search Console and reported in the Performance report within the Web search type.
  <br><sub>`D3-C498` · Google Search Central · annotates Day 3, Lightning session L: Understanding SERPs and your users · is the documentation · [AI features and your website](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features) · Extends [D3-C438](../../40-sessions/day3/D3-S12-inside-search-console-what-s-new-how-to-use-it.md) · Used by `DEV-MON-07`</sub>

- **[Docs]** In an August 2025 post, Google's Head of Search wrote that total organic click volume from Google Search to websites had been relatively stable year-over-year and that Google was sending slightly more quality clicks (clicks where users do not quickly click back) than a year earlier; the post gave no figures.
  <br><sub>`D3-C506` · Google blog (6 August 2025) · annotates Day 3, Lightning session L: Understanding SERPs and your users · is the documentation · [AI in Search is driving more queries and higher quality clicks](https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/search/ai-search-driving-more-queries-higher-quality-clicks/)</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's AI features guide says clicks from search results pages with AI Overviews are higher quality, meaning users are more likely to spend more time on the site.
  <br><sub>`D3-C534` · Google Search Central · annotates Day 3, Lightning session L: Understanding SERPs and your users · is the documentation · [AI features and your website](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features)</sub>

- **[Docs]** Beyond Search Console, Google's AI features guide suggests tracking conversions and time spent on the site in tools such as Google Analytics to understand the value of traffic from AI features.
  <br><sub>`D3-C535` · Google Search Central · annotates Day 3, Lightning session L: Understanding SERPs and your users · is the documentation · [AI features and your website](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features) · Extends [D1-C062](../../40-sessions/day1/D1-S03-how-search-works-and-where-s-ai.md)</sub>

- **[Docs]** A May 2025 Search Central blog post advised site owners to look at the overall value of visits from Search rather than focusing too much on clicks, using indicators of conversion such as sales, sign-ups, a more engaged audience or information lookups about the business.
  <br><sub>`D3-C536` · Search Central blog (21 May 2025) · annotates Day 3, Lightning session L: Understanding SERPs and your users · is the documentation · [Top ways to ensure your content performs well in Google's AI experiences on Search](https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2025/05/succeeding-in-ai-search) · Extends [D1-C057](../../40-sessions/day1/D1-S03-how-search-works-and-where-s-ai.md)</sub>

## Analysis

- **[Analysis]** After a migration, judge success by the new domain's indexing and traffic in Search Console rather than by a site: query on the old domain, and keep the old domain's redirects in place long term so searches for the old brand still reach the new site.
  <br><sub>`D2-C358` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 2, Handling web duplication · Used by `DEV-CAN-09`</sub>

- **[Analysis]** The 304-day median recovery a community speaker cited from an unnamed study and Google's site move guide (a few weeks or more for a medium-sized site until Google shows the new URLs, longer for larger sites) measure different things: indexing can switch within weeks while traffic recovery can take far longer, so plan and report on both.
  <br><sub>`D2-C915` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 2, Lightning session E: Managing Duplicates and Site Moves · [How to move a site](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/site-move-with-url-changes)</sub>

- **[Analysis]** Check AI Overviews and AI Mode with native-language queries in each target market, not with translated English keywords, and compare with the country breakdown of Search Console's generative AI performance report; topics where competitors are cited and you are not point to missing or weak local content.
  <br><sub>`D2-C607` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 2, Focusing on Internationalisation and Localisation · [Introducing Search Generative AI performance reports in Search Console](https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2026/06/gen-ai-performance-reports) · Extends [D1-C124](../../40-sessions/day1/D1-S03-how-search-works-and-where-s-ai.md) · Used by `DEV-MON-07`</sub>

- **[Analysis]** Google Trends cannot show demand that reaches people through the Discover feed, so Discover visibility has to be judged from Search Console's Discover performance report rather than from Trends.
  <br><sub>`D2-C751` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 2, Google Trends</sub>

- **[Analysis]** No Google documentation states that fan-out queries stay out of Search Console, but the docs fit the stage statement: the Performance report counts AI Overviews and AI Mode under the user's own queries, and the Generative AI reports have no query dimension.
  <br><sub>`D3-C095` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 3, Making sense of users' queries · [What are impressions, position, and clicks?](https://support.google.com/webmasters/answer/7042828?hl=en), [Introducing Search Generative AI performance reports in Search Console](https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2026/06/gen-ai-performance-reports), [AI features and your website](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features)</sub>

- **[Analysis]** Impressions and business value can diverge sharply, so judge each article by its clicks and conversions, not by its impressions alone, before deciding which content to expand or retire.
  <br><sub>`D3-C125` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 3, Lightning session K: Facets of quality</sub>

- **[Analysis]** The case-study figures were said on stage without a photographed slide, a data source or absolute click numbers, and together they imply a click-through rate nearly 1,000 times higher on the niche article, so use them as an illustration, not a benchmark.
  <br><sub>`D3-C126` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 3, Lightning session K: Facets of quality</sub>

- **[Analysis]** Search Console's generative AI performance reports count impressions only, with no clicks and no query dimension (Google documents the Search report for AI Overviews and AI Mode, plus a separate Discover report), so measure visits that follow AI answers with your own analytics.
  <br><sub>`D3-C441` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 3, Inside Search Console: What’s New & How to Use It · Used by `DEV-MON-07`</sub>

- **[Analysis]** A query reaches Search Console's Performance report only through an impression, so queries cannot come before impressions; what rises first after a publish or refresh is the number of queries with a few impressions each, before total impressions and clicks grow noticeably.
  <br><sub>`D3-C484` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 3, Lightning session L: Understanding SERPs and your users</sub>

- **[Analysis]** Pages that do better in AI answers than in classic results do not refute Google's line that optimising for people is optimising for generative AI Search, since the comparison mixed Google's AI features with third-party LLMs; measure each surface separately, per page, before deciding what to change.
  <br><sub>`D3-C497` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 3, Lightning session L: Understanding SERPs and your users · [Optimizing your website for generative AI features on Google Search](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/ai-optimization-guide) · Extends [D1-C058](../../40-sessions/day1/D1-S03-how-search-works-and-where-s-ai.md)</sub>

- **[Analysis]** Because Google says anonymized queries are left out whenever a filter is applied, branded plus non-branded exports should not be expected to add up to the unfiltered chart totals; tell an LLM that sums filtered exports that the gap is expected, not missing data.
  <br><sub>`D3-C500` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 3, Lightning session L: Understanding SERPs and your users · [A deep dive into Search Console performance data filtering and limits](https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2022/10/performance-data-deep-dive)</sub>

- **[Analysis]** Before feeding a branded versus non-branded split to an LLM, spot-check a sample of queries in each group, since Google's AI-assisted classification can misidentify queries; on URL-path or subdomain properties, where the filter is unavailable, a regex query filter is the fallback.
  <br><sub>`D3-C501` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 3, Lightning session L: Understanding SERPs and your users · [Introducing the branded queries filter in Search Console](https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2025/11/search-console-branded-filter) · Extends [D3-C435](../../40-sessions/day3/D3-S12-inside-search-console-what-s-new-how-to-use-it.md)</sub>

- **[Analysis]** The click decline described on stage is what many individual sites report, while Google's published position (August 2025) is that total organic clicks are relatively stable but shifting between sites, with fewer clicks for quick-answer questions; neither side gave figures, so measure the trend per site and per query type rather than assuming a market-wide fall.
  <br><sub>`D3-C508` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 3, Lightning session L: Understanding SERPs and your users · [AI in Search is driving more queries and higher quality clicks](https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/search/ai-search-driving-more-queries-higher-quality-clicks/)</sub>

- **[Analysis]** The community speaker's figures (paid search click-through rate up 36%, organic sessions halved, a record month) come from one unpublished test of one unnamed brand with no stated period or baseline; use them as an illustration, not as a benchmark.
  <br><sub>`D3-C541` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 3, Lightning session L: Understanding SERPs and your users</sub>

- **[Analysis]** Google's own line on Day 1 was to measure success by metrics that matter to the business, and its Generative AI performance report shows impressions but no clicks; together with the community talk this argues for a report that puts organic next to direct, branded paid search, conversions and revenue.
  <br><sub>`D3-C542` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 3, Lightning session L: Understanding SERPs and your users · Extends [D1-C057](../../40-sessions/day1/D1-S03-how-search-works-and-where-s-ai.md) · Extends [D1-C124](../../40-sessions/day1/D1-S03-how-search-works-and-where-s-ai.md)</sub>

- **[Analysis]** For a site's own test of AI visibility, write down the period, the baseline and every other marketing change before starting, and compare a test area with a similar control area; paid click-through rate and direct and branded traffic are the signals the community speaker watched.
  <br><sub>`D3-C543` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 3, Lightning session L: Understanding SERPs and your users</sub>

- **[Analysis]** Google's finding that AI users visit more brand websites is Google's own research; check it against your own data, such as branded and direct traffic in analytics and the Generative AI performance report in Search Console, before planning on it.
  <br><sub>`D3-C596` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 3, Mastering the messy middle</sub>

## Built on these claims

The items of the developer and content kits that rest on this topic's claims.

- Requirement `DEV-AIF-03`: Structure content for readers instead of splitting it into small chunks for AI
- Requirement `DEV-CAN-09`: Keep migration redirects in place long term and judge a move in Search Console, not with site: queries
- Requirement `DEV-CAN-10`: Redirect an old URL only to a page with the same intent, and return 404 or 410 when there is none
- Requirement `DEV-MON-07`: Track AI feature visibility in the Generative AI performance report
- Requirement `DEV-MON-08`: Set up the Search Console bulk data export to BigQuery on large sites
- Requirement `DEV-MON-09`: Add the brand's YouTube, Instagram, TikTok and X accounts to Search Console as platform properties
- Glossary term *Branded queries filter*
- Glossary term *Downstream impact*
- Glossary term *Generative AI performance report*
- Glossary term *Query fan-out*
